about: Real neuron shapes and protein shapes used in the 3D lesson visuals (Neurons, Synaptic transmission). Neuron files are SWC reconstructions downloaded from NeuroMorpho.Org on 2026-11-15 (CNG versions) and simplified for the web (fewer points along unbranched stretches; branch points, end points and the cell body kept). Protein surfaces are smoothed, low-poly surfaces computed by us from the atom coordinates of public Protein Data Bank entries.

neurons.used_for: The generic neuron (Neurons lesson steps 1-5 and recap); the postsynaptic neuron in the summation demo (Synaptic transmission step 6).
neurons.archive: Allen Cell Types (Allen Institute for Brain Science)
neurons.brain_region: neocortex, temporal lobe, middle temporal gyrus (left), layer 2/3
neurons.notes: Tissue removed during neurosurgery (epilepsy), studied in a brain slice. Dendrites and axon reconstructed (NeuroMorpho integrity: 'Dendrites & Axon Complete'); the axon is cut where it leaves the slice. No myelin in the reconstruction: myelin sheaths and nodes of Ranvier are drawn along the main axon and labelled as added. The nucleus is drawn. Thin branches are drawn at least about 1 pixel wide so they stay visible. Original data © Allen Institute for Brain Science (Allen Cell Types Database); the Allen Institute's own terms allow non-commercial use only.
neurons.original_paper: Berg J, Sorensen SA, Ting JT, Miller JA, et al. (2021) Human neocortical expansion involves glutamatergic neuron diversification. Nature 598:151-158. doi:10.1038/s41586-021-03813-8

neurons.used_for: Motor neuron (Neurons lesson step 9 and the reflex arc).
neurons.brain_region: spinal cord, lumbar L4-L5, ventral horn
neurons.cell_type: alpha motor neuron projecting to the gastrocnemius muscle
neurons.notes: Filled in vivo. Dendrites complete; the axon is only reconstructed inside the spinal cord. The axon's continuation through the ventral root to a muscle, its myelin and the muscle are drawn and labelled as drawn.
neurons.original_paper: Rotterman TM, Nardelli P, Cope TC, Alvarez FJ (2014) Normal distribution of VGLUT1 synapses on spinal motoneuron dendrites and their reorganization after nerve injury. Journal of Neuroscience 34(10):3475-3492. doi:10.1523/JNEUROSCI.4768-13.2014

neurons.used_for: Relay neuron (Neurons lesson step 8 and the reflex arc).
neurons.notes: A CNS interneuron used as the example 'relay neuron'. Reconstructed from a parasagittal slice (integrity 'Dendrites & Axon Moderate'). It is turned on its side in the 'three types' view and turned and resized to fit in the reflex arc.
neurons.original_paper: Dickie AC, Bell AM, Iwagaki N, et al., Todd AJ (2019) Morphological and functional properties distinguish the substance P and gastrin-releasing peptide subsets of excitatory interneuron in the spinal cord dorsal horn. Pain 160(2):442-462. doi:10.1097/j.pain.0000000000001406

neurons.used_for: The receptor ending of the sensory neuron (Neurons lesson step 7 and the reflex arc).
neurons.brain_region: peripheral nervous system, dorsal root ganglion neuron (its ending in the skin)
neurons.notes: Only the branching ending in the skin was reconstructed (no cell body, no diameters). NeuroMorpho.Org has no complete reconstruction of a mammalian dorsal root ganglion (pseudo-unipolar) neuron with its cell body, peripheral and central branches (searched 2026-11-15: DRG entries are skin endings, cultured cells, or soma-only). So the long fibre, the cell body in the ganglion, the T-shaped junction and the short central branch are drawn, and labelled as drawn. NeuroMorpho.Org records this tracing as an axon arbor: the branching ending of the sensory fibre. AQA calls the long fibre from the receptor a dendrite, so the lesson labels it that way, with a note that scientists often call it an axon.
neurons.original_paper: Wu H, Williams J, Nathans J (2012) Morphologic diversity of cutaneous sensory afferents revealed by genetically directed sparse labeling. eLife 1:e00181. doi:10.7554/eLife.00181

proteins.licence: Protein Data Bank (wwPDB) data are free of all copyright restrictions (CC0 1.0 public domain dedication). Please cite the structure's primary publication.
proteins.method: Heavy atoms of the protein chains only (antibodies, nanobodies, sugars, drugs and water removed). Gaussian density on a 2 Å grid, marching-cubes surface, coarse sampling for a low-poly mesh. Membrane proteins were oriented with their membrane slab horizontal (hydrophobic-band search) and the outside of the cell up.

proteins.note: These four proteins come from different kinds of synapse. They are shown together as examples of a receptor, a transporter and an enzyme; no single real synapse has all four.

drawn_not_data: Myelin sheaths and nodes of Ranvier (no reconstruction includes myelin).
Terminal buttons: a small swelling drawn at the end of every traced axon branch (the tracings do not record them; some branch ends are where the axon was cut by the slice).
The nucleus inside the cell body.
The 'next neuron' dendrite at the terminal button, and the width of the gap.
The sensory neuron's fibre, cell body and T-junction; the motor axon outside the spinal cord; the muscle, skin, nerves and spinal cord.
The synapse membranes, vesicles and neurotransmitter molecules (molecules drawn about 10 times bigger than real and far fewer).
